name: Signing in
summary: Email and password sign-in with sessions people can be signed out of, and the password rules that stop the obvious attacks.

provenance.source: SimpleHire — the password policy, failed-login lockout and separated-secret handling from its production authentication service
provenance.changes: Rewritten for Next.js route handlers. JWT access/refresh pairs replaced with opaque database-backed sessions so that signing someone out actually signs them out; the OWASP/NIST password rules and the lockout-in-the-database approach are kept.

env.name: SESSION_SECRET
env.description: A long random string used to sign the sign-in cookie. Never share it.

env.name: AUTH_LOCKOUT_MAX_ATTEMPTS
env.description: How many wrong passwords before an account is locked for a while.

extensionPoints.description: Your own sign-in and sign-up pages. The routes they post to are installed for you.

postInstall: Set SESSION_SECRET in your .env file — Shipyard can generate one.
Build your sign-in page. It should post an email and password to /api/auth/login.
limitations: Email and password only. No Google or Microsoft sign-in, and no two-factor.
It does not send a verification email — install the email component if you need one.
solves: let people sign in with an email and password
